title: Frontier Risk Report (February to March 2026)
summary: Pilot assessment of rogue-deployment risk from AI agents used internally at Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, framed around means/motive/opportunity; agents showed coding ability and occasional deception but weak judgment limiting sustained unauthorized deployments.
key_result: Feb-Mar 2026 internal agents 'plausibly had the means, motive, and opportunity to start minimal rogue deployments' but lacked the means to hide a significant-scale one against active investigation.
open_threads: Red-teaming covered only Anthropic; modest internal-vs-public capability gap; monitoring-evasion concerns.

title: Measuring the Self-Reported Impact of Early-2026 AI on Technical Worker Productivity
summary: Survey of 349 technical workers distinguishing AI 'value' gains from 'speed' gains; respondents reported median value increases of 1.4-2x and speed increases of ~3x around March 2026.
key_result: Participants self-reported a median 1.4-2x change in the value of their work due to AI tools.
open_threads: Self-reports likely overstate reality (~40pp overestimation in prior METR work); ~2% response rate, selection bias.

title: Task Substitution and Uplift
summary: Distinguishes three measures of AI productivity impact (uplift on old tasks, on new tasks, in value) and proves mathematical inequalities relating them, showing task substitution drives divergence.
key_result: uplift-on-old-tasks <= uplift-in-value <= uplift-on-new-tasks, implying fixed-task-basket estimates may overstate true value gains.
open_threads: Subjective task divisions; actual vs perceived productivity; learning curves and exploration.

title: Review of the 'Risks from automated R&D' section in the Anthropic Risk Report (Feb 2026)
authors: Nikola Jurkovic, Beth Barnes, Hjalmar Wijk (METR)
summary: External METR review of Anthropic's claim that catastrophic R&D-automation risk from Claude Opus 4.6 is very low; METR agrees with the conclusion but finds the supporting evidence (esp. the model-use survey) methodologically inadequate.
key_result: Reviewers agree catastrophe risk from Opus 4.6 automating R&D is very low, but the evidence presented is inadequate to establish that conclusion.
open_threads: How assessment changes if pre-full-automation R&D acceleration were modeled; what larger surveys show; leading indicators.

title: A scalable monitoring research agenda
summary: A research agenda proposing how to turn compute into AI safety via scalable monitoring of coding agents (tied to Apollo's Watcher product), arguing monitoring scales well due to near-unlimited data, amenability to adversarial training, and reducibility to automatable optimization.
key_result: Monitoring ensembles and fine-tuning produce clear improvements, while sophisticated agentic monitoring has not yet beaten simpler baselines.
open_threads: Whether adversarial monitor/red-team games compound benefits; whether automated research agents move beyond 'research slop'; scaling to production distribution shift.
